result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.gwas_pipeline()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Run a GWAS-style network analysis pipeline. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L24753-L24954){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.gwas_pipeline( scores, smooth_alpha=0.5, smooth_max_iter=100, community_method="louvain", community_resolution=1.0, enrichment_attr=None, enrichment_labels=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![GWAS network pipeline](/assets/graphs/gwas-pipeline.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The eight-gene network after the pipeline: raw scores of 4.0 on G1, G2, G3 and 0.5 elsewhere are smoothed over the network, so every gene is shaded by its smoothed score and the signal leaks onto G4. Louvain then splits the network into module 1, G1 to G4, and module 0, G5 to G8, drawn as gray regions. The table ranks the modules by mean smoothed score, 3.05 for module 1 and 0.57 for module 0." width="100%"} Chains three steps: 1. network smoothing: propagates raw scores (e.g., -log10 p-values) over the graph to denoise using neighborhood context. 2. community detection: partitions the graph into modules. This step uses only the network structure; the scores do not influence the partition. 3. module scoring: computes mean smoothed score per module and ranks modules by aggregate signal. Optionally, if a positive set of nodes is given (through `enrichment_attr=` or `enrichment_labels=`), computes a fold enrichment for each community to test for over-representation of those nodes. The pipeline answers a common question in network genetics: which groups of interacting genes carry the strongest association signal? Single-gene statistics are noisy, and a module where many neighboring genes are moderately associated can be more convincing than one isolated hit. Smoothing (step 1) is the same computation as `network_smooth()` with `tol=1e-6`, and community detection (step 2) calls `cmty_louvain()` or `cmty_walktrap()`. Use those methods directly if you need more control over either step. Typical uses: - ranking gene modules by GWAS or differential-expression signal - finding candidate pathways for follow-up from a list of per-gene scores - checking whether high-scoring modules are also enriched for known disease genes Nothing is written to the graph: the smoothed scores and community assignments are only returned. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [scores]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping node IDs to raw scores (e.g., GWAS -log10(p-value) or differential expression fold change). Nodes not in the dictionary start at `0.0`. Higher scores should mean stronger signal, because modules are ranked by descending mean score. [smooth_alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.5]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Smoothing strength between `0` and `1`, as in `network_smooth()`. The default is `0.5`. Higher values give more weight to network neighbors; `0` skips smoothing and uses the raw scores. [smooth_max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of smoothing iterations. The default is `100`, which is normally enough for the smoothing to converge. [community_method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["louvain"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Community detection method: `"louvain"` (the default) or `"walktrap"`. Walktrap only works on undirected graphs. [community_resolution]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Resolution parameter for community detection, passed to `cmty_louvain()`. The default is `1.0`; higher values give more, smaller modules and lower values give fewer, larger ones. It is ignored when `community_method="walktrap"`. [enrichment_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of a node attribute marking the "positive" nodes for enrichment testing, such as a `known_disease_gene` flag: nodes whose value is truthy are positive, and nodes lacking the attribute are not. Giving it switches on the enrichment step. The default, `None`, skips it unless `enrichment_labels=` is given. [enrichment_labels]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Alternatively, an explicit list of node IDs to use as the positive set. Giving it switches on the enrichment step. Use either this or `enrichment_attr=`, not both. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A dictionary with: - `smoothed_scores`: dict mapping node IDs to smoothed values. - `communities`: dict mapping community ID to list of node IDs. - `module_scores`: dict mapping community ID to mean smoothed score, sorted descending. - `enrichment` (if requested): dict mapping community ID to the fold enrichment of positive nodes, i.e., the number of positive nodes in the community divided by the number expected if they were spread evenly. A value of `1.0` means no enrichment, values above `1.0` mean over-representation, and `0.0` means none present. This is a ratio, not a p-value. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `community_method=` is not `"louvain"` or `"walktrap"`, if `smooth_alpha=` is outside `[0, 1]`, or if both `enrichment_attr=` and `enrichment_labels=` are given. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Three four-gene cliques are joined in a chain. Only the first clique (`g0` to `g3`) has strong scores. Louvain recovers the three cliques as modules, and the module containing the scored genes comes first in `module_scores` with a far higher mean: ::: {#a8a5c209 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph() g.add_nodes([f"g{i}" for i in range(12)]) for block in [range(0, 4), range(4, 8), range(8, 12)]: for x in block: for y in block: if x < y: g.add_edge(f"g{x}", f"g{y}") g.add_edge("g3", "g4").add_edge("g7", "g8") scores = {g.get_id_from_label(f"g{i}"): (5.0 if i < 4 else 0.5) for i in range(12)} result = g.gwas_pipeline(scores) {cid: round(s, 3) for cid, s in result["module_scores"].items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {0: 4.76, 1: 0.735, 2: 0.505} ``` ::: ::: The module that comes second is the middle clique: it is next to the scored clique, so a little of their signal leaks into it. Each module's members are listed in `communities`: ::: {#98f29d5f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} { cid: sorted(g.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in members) for cid, members in result["communities"].items() } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {2: ['g10', 'g11', 'g8', 'g9'], 1: ['g4', 'g5', 'g6', 'g7'], 0: ['g0', 'g1', 'g2', 'g3']} ``` ::: ::: Supplying a set of known genes adds a fold-enrichment value per module. Two of the three known genes fall in the first clique, twice what an even spread would put there: ::: {#b6c7ff79 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} known = [g.get_id_from_label(label) for label in ["g0", "g1", "g5"]] result = g.gwas_pipeline(scores, enrichment_labels=known) result["enrichment"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {2: 0.0, 1: 1.0, 0: 2.0} ``` ::: ::: The same positive set can come from a node attribute instead, here a `known` flag: ::: {#9ec9e833 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} g.set_node_attrs("known", {nid: True for nid in known}) g.gwas_pipeline(scores, enrichment_attr="known")["enrichment"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {2: 0.0, 1: 1.0, 0: 2.0} ``` ::: :::
